# Jev no ENEM: Avaliação Psicométrica e Calibração de Modelos System One no ENEM 2025 [![Kaggle Dataset](https://img.shields.io/badge/Kaggle-Dataset%20ENEM%202025-blue?logo=kaggle)](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/serenozin/prova-enem-2025/data) [![Architecture](https://img.shields.io/badge/Architecture-System%20One%20(TypeSafe)-emerald)](https://typesafe.ai) [![Protocol](https://img.shields.io/badge/Spec--Driven-Analysis-indigo)](./spec/experimental_protocol.yaml) Primeiro benchmark público avaliando o modelo **Jev (TypeSafe AI)** em exames padronizados brasileiros. Investigamos a transição do paradigma autorregressivo tradicional (LLMs generativas) para o paradigma **System One** (decisão tipada paralela, latência ultrabaixa e calibração de confiança via RLCD) aplicado aos Cadernos do **ENEM 2025** (Caderno Azul - 1º e 2º Dias). --- ## 🎯 Destaques do Projeto - **Paradigma System One vs Generativo:** Avaliação empírica entre decisão direta tipada via primitiva `Choice` (70–500 ms) versus geração discursiva token a token de LLMs abertas. - **Fundamentação Psicométrica:** Alinhamento com a Teoria de Resposta ao Item (TRI / Modelo Logístico 3-PL) do INEP e análise da atratividade de distratores. - **Calibração Formal de Incerteza:** Acurácia não é tudo. Mensuramos *Expected Calibration Error* (ECE) e *Brier Score Multiclasse* para verificar se a certeza do modelo reflete sua precisão empírica. - **Engenharia de Estado:** Comparativo entre o estado bruto transcrito (`JEV-RAW`) e o estado estruturado/decomposto (`JEV-STATE`), mitigando *context rot*. - **Produto Final Interativo:** Dashboard analítico hospedado em **GitHub Pages** consumindo diretamente dados consolidados em JSON. --- ## 📊 Dataset no Kaggle Para seguir as melhores práticas de engenharia de dados e manter o repositório leve, os dados tabulares da prova do ENEM 2025 estão hospedados publicamente no Kaggle: 👉 **[Kaggle: Prova ENEM 2025 - Dataset Completo](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/serenozin/prova-enem-2025/data)** - `gabarito.csv`: Gabarito oficial do 1º Dia (`numero;lingua_opcao;gabarito`). - `enem_2025_d1_questoes_gabarito.csv`: Questões unificadas com alternativas A–E (Linguagens e Humanas). - `gabarito_d2.csv`: Gabarito oficial do 2º Dia (`numero;area;gabarito`). - `enem_2025_d2_questoes_gabarito.csv`: Questões unificadas com alternativas A–E (Natureza e Matemática). --- ## 🔬 Análise de Consistência e Dinâmica do Escape (`INVALIDO`) O benchmark avaliou o modelo em duas rodadas experimentais: 1. **Com Escape (`INVALIDO`):** O modelo pôde escolher entre A, B, C, D, E ou se abster quando julgasse as alternativas insuficientes ou ambíguas. 2. **Sem Escape (Decisão Forçada A–E):** O modelo foi compelido a distribuir probabilidades exclusivamente no espaço de respostas válidas. ### Achados Empíricos de Estabilidade: * **Concordância Intra-Modelo de 97.7%:** Nos 86 itens em que o Jev tomou uma decisão firme na primeira rodada (sem marcar `INVALIDO`), ele repetiu **exatamente a mesma alternativa em 84 itens** na segunda rodada. * **O Escape como Filtro Efetivo de Risco:** - Nos itens que o modelo aceitou responder espontaneamente, a acurácia foi de **78.8%**. - Nos itens que o modelo havia rejeitado (`INVALIDO`), ao ser forçado a chutar na segunda rodada, a acurácia foi de **35.5%**. Isso comprova que a rota de fuga drenou itens de alta entropia e incerteza real. * **Superação do Chute Aleatório:** Mesmo no conjunto de maior dificuldade/rejeição (onde a acurácia foi de 35.5%), o modelo superou com folga a linha de base do chute puramente aleatório (**20.0%**). * **Decomposição do Erro de Calibração (ECE):** - No teste com escape, como o `INVALIDO` foi contabilizado como erro frente ao gabarito do INEP, o ECE computou em **0.275**. - Ao remover a penalização do escape e avaliar a calibração estrita nas alternativas da prova, o ECE caiu para **0.078**, evidenciando que a confiança declarada pelo RLCD acompanha a acurácia empírica em todas as faixas de probabilidade. ### 🏆 Quadro Comparativo Consolidado (182 Itens Válidos): | Modelo / Arquitetura | Paradigma | Acurácia Global | Linguagens | Humanas | Natureza | Matemática | ECE (Calibração) | | :--- | :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | | **Jev 1.13.0 (Sem Escape)** | System One (Primitiva Choice) | **56.6%** (103/182) | **78.0%** | **73.3%** | 46.5% | 25.0% | **0.078** | | **NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Super 120B** | Generativo Autorregressivo (MoE) | **56.0%** (102/182) | 64.0% | 64.4% | **53.5%** | **40.9%** | 0.235 | | **NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning** | Generativo Autorregressivo (MoE) | **46.2%** (84/182) | 62.0% | 53.3% | 41.9% | 25.0% | 0.228 | | *Jev 1.13.0 (Com Escape - Acurácia Efetiva)* | System One (Filtro Ativo) | *78.8% (70/89)* | *78.8%* | *82.1%* | *77.3%* | *66.7%* | *0.275 (penalizado)* | --- ## 💡 Conclusões Empíricas do Estudo A análise dos resultados experimentais consolidados revela três eixos conclusivos centrais: ### 1. Acurácia Global: Empate Técnico entre Paradigmas Na pontuação bruta sem escape (182 itens válidos), o **Jev 1.13.0** obteve **56.6%** (103 acertos), estabelecendo um empate técnico rigoroso com o **Nemotron 3 Super 120B**, que atingiu **56.0%** (102 acertos). Ambos os modelos superaram substancialmente a linha de base puramente aleatória (**20.0%** para 5 alternativas) e o modelo compacto **Nemotron 3.5 Lightning** (**46.2%**). Isso demonstra que uma arquitetura discriminativa ultracompacta (*System One*) com saída tipada direta atinge o mesmo patamar resolutivo de um modelo generativo massivo de 120 bilhões de parâmetros no exame nacional brasileiro. ### 2. Perfil Cognitivo Segmentado por Área As duas arquiteturas manifestaram especializações complementares bastante nítidas: * **Domínio Textual e Interpretativo (Dia 1):** O Jev superou largamente as LLMs em **Linguagens e Códigos (78.0% vs 64.0%)** e **Ciências Humanas (73.3% vs 64.4%)**. Esse resultado confirma que o processamento discriminativo paralelo do Jev assimila com grande acuidade o contexto discursivo e a semântica em língua portuguesa, desarmando distratores do ENEM com eficácia superior. * **Raciocínio Simbólico e Quantitativo (Dia 2):** O Nemotron 120B obteve vantagem em **Matemática (40.9% vs 25.0%)** e **Ciências da Natureza (53.5% vs 46.5%)**. O Jev, sem ferramentas acessórias (como calculadoras ou interpretadores de código) e com representação em texto puro sem formatação LaTeX avançada, sofre degradação em problemas que demandam encadeamento aritmético em múltiplos passos, operando em Matemática no nível basal do chute estatístico. ### 3. Calibração de Incerteza e Estabilidade: O Diferencial Qualitativo A grande distinção prática do benchmark não reside apenas na acurácia, mas na **confiabilidade da incerteza**: * **Alta Calibração do Jev (ECE = 0.078):** Diferente dos modelos generativos tradicionais, a probabilidade atribuída pelo Jev (via RLCD) acompanha a taxa de acerto observada ao longo de todos os intervalos de confiança. Quando o Jev declara confiança entre 80% e 100%, sua precisão empírica é de **89.1%**; quando opera entre 40% e 60%, sua taxa de acerto é de **50.0%**. * **Superconfiança Crônica das LLMs (ECE = 0.228 – 0.235):** Os modelos Nemotron exibiram a descalibração típica de geradores de texto autorregressivos. No intervalo de 80% a 100% de confiança declarada, a acurácia do Nemotron 120B despencou para apenas **62.9%**, emitindo certezas categóricas em dezenas de respostas incorretas. * **Consistência Intra-Modelo de 97.7%:** Nos 86 itens em que o Jev optou por responder na rodada com escape, ele manteve exatamente a mesma alternativa em 84 itens na rodada de decisão forçada. Além disso, a rota de escape provou filtrar com precisão os itens de maior entropia cognitiva: ao forçar o modelo a responder os itens que antes rejeitava, a taxa de acerto caiu para 35.5%, confirmando que a abstenção não era ruído estocástico, mas detecção real de baixa previsibilidade. --- ## 🏗️ Arquitetura do Benchmark O fluxo de dados e inferência opera em pipeline modular, desde a extração dos cadernos oficiais até a publicação analítica interativa: ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph INGESTION["1. readme_preview:
# hermes-model-routing

A Hermes skill for routing work between a **smart** (planner/frontier) model and an
**implementer** — including a **validated decision gate** that classifies a task brief in
~0.5 s for ~$0.00002.

- Hermes has no single "planner model / implementer model" pair — the split is made at the
  **delegation boundary** or by switching models. Three wiring patterns inside.
- The gate: **Jev** (`typesafe/jev-1.13`, TypeSafe's System One decision model) via
  OpenRouter's alpha decisions endpoint. Measured on 74 real task briefs (2026-09-21):
  **82.4% argmax / 89.2% holdout** at a fitted threshold (majority baseline 60.8%),
  0 errors, ~$0.000023 per decision.
- A rival zero-shot classifier (**laya**) failed the same task (52.7% — below the majority
  baseline). The full evaluation protocol is included so you can validate any gate on
  *your* briefs before wiring it.

## Install (Hermes)

```bash
# the skill
cp -r hermes-model-routing ~/.hermes/skills/autonomous-ai-agents/
# the gate CLI
cp hermes-model-routing/scripts/jev_route.py ~/.local/bin/jev-route && chmod +x ~/.local/bin/jev-route
export OPENROUTER_API_KEY=...        # a standard OpenRouter key
```

The skill is picked up at the next session start (or run `/reload-skills`).

## Quick start

```bash
jev-route "Diagnose why nightly CI fails intermittently on the release branch"
# → smart   P(smart)=0.99  depth=1.96 ...

jev-route --json "Renumber migration 101 to 102 and update the docs"
jev-route --threshold 0.62 "borderline brief"     # conservative mode (~89% holdout)
jev-route --batch briefs.jsonl                    # {id?, text|goal, label?} per line
```

Route `smart` → keep it in the main loop / frontier model. Route `implementer` → delegate to
a pinned subagent or a coding CLI.

## Files

- `SKILL.md` — the skill: wiring patterns, gate usage, pitfalls
- `scripts/jev_route.py` — the gate CLI (stdlib only; deploy as `jev-route`)
- `scripts/laya_route_probe.py` — the failed rival's re-runnable probe (kept for the protocol)
- `references/jev-api.md` — API shape, access routes, caveats
- `references/routing-gate-eval.md` — the evaluation protocol (mine → label → fit/holdout)
- `references/laya-decision-gate.md` — the laya result in full

## Notes

- The OpenRouter decisions endpoint is **alpha** — if a future run 404s, re-verify with a
  smoke call and check OpenRouter's docs for a new path.
- The accuracy numbers are for the question wording in `scripts/jev_route.py` — keep it
  verbatim.

readme_preview:
# Hacker News Judge

The most-discussed threads on Hacker News (only threads with 6+ comments, most comments first), each read comment by comment by [Jev](https://typesafe.ai) and reduced to a single verdict, served live from [Neon Lakebase Postgres](https://neon.com). Full-text search over the whole corpus is included, with BM25 ranking. The UI is styled to feel like a native part of news.ycombinator.com.

## Thread Judge (Jev)

Judged threads render inline on the home page as a Jev verdict strip, and a "The finding" card in the right column is computed live over every judged thread. Each verdict is produced by [Jev](https://typesafe.ai) (TypeSafe System One): every comment (up to 400 per thread, top-level reactions first) is sent to Jev on its own and comes back with a _typed_ judgment: a categorical stance (`support` / `critical` / `neutral`), an ordinal substance score, a 0..1 quotability scalar, and whether it raises an open question. Jev never writes prose, so the verdict card is assembled deterministically from those numbers, and every quote on it is a real comment Jev flagged. Open [`/item/{id}`](src/app/item/[id]/page.tsx) for a judged thread to see the card plus a per-comment stance badge on each judged comment.

Any unjudged thread can be judged on demand: the button on the thread calls [`POST /api/judge/:id`](src/app/api/judge/[id]/route.ts), which scores it with Jev and persists the verdict. New judges are rate limited to `DAILY_JUDGE_LIMIT` (10) per IP per day, tracked in a `judge_rate_limit` row in the same database (see [`rate-limit.ts`](src/lib/rate-limit.ts)). Already-judged threads return the stored verdict without spending quota, and a failed judge is refunded. The request-path pipeline is [`src/lib/judge.ts`](src/lib/judge.ts).

Scoring is additive. The judgments go into nullable `jev_*` columns on `items` (per comment) and a `jev_verdict` jsonb blob on the story row. No existing column or value is touched. To score threads in bulk offline instead of on demand:

```bash
npm run db:judge            # score threads not yet scored
npm run db:judge -- --force # re-score all of them
```

Set `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` in `.env` first. The batch pipeline is in [`scripts/judge-threads.ts`](scripts/judge-threads.ts). The constants `TOP_N`, `CAP` and `CONCURRENCY` at the top tune coverage and speed.

## Design notes

- **[Next.js 16](https://nextjs.org)**: App Router, React Server Components, streaming SSR. Every page ships its shell (masthead, search box) instantly and streams the data through a React `<Suspense>` boundary keyed by the query, so navigating shows a skeleton right away instead of freezing on the previous results. The match count is a second, nested boundary that fills in after the results.
- **[Neon Lakebase Postgres](https://neon.com)** over the `@neondatabase/serverless` HTTP driver. Each request is a stateless SQL-over-HTTP round trip with no connection pool. The compute is pinned (see [`neon.ts`](neon.ts)) so there is no scale-to-zero cold start on the first query.
- **Postgres is the search engine.** `lakebase_text` with a `lakebase_bm25` index does corpus-aware BM25 ranking inside the database.
- **Per-type partial BM25 indexes.** The corpus is 85% comments, so a single shared BM25 index is a trap: it scores only its top `lakebase_bm25.default_limit` candidates (1000 by default) and _then_ applies the `type` filter, silently dropping most stories and nearly all jobs before you see them. Each searchable type gets its own **partial** index whose predicate matches the query's `WHERE` clause:

  ```sql
  CREATE INDEX items_story_bm25   ON items USING lakebase_bm25 (search_tsv) WHERE type = 'story'   AND NOT deleted AND NOT dead;
  CREATE INDEX items_comment_bm25 ON items USING lakebase_bm25 (search_tsv) WHERE type = 'comment' AND NOT deleted AND NOT dead;
  CREATE INDEX items_job_bm25     ON items USING lakebase_bm25 (search_tsv) WHERE type = 'job'     AND NOT deleted AND NOT dead;
  ```

  Ranking and counting now run over the requested type alone, so results are complete and correctly ordered at any page. `all` and the long-tail types (poll, pollopt) fall back to the full-corpus `items_search_bm25` index. The candidate limit is set per query inside a transaction, big enough to cover the page being read and opened to the cap when a residual `by`/`since` filter runs afterward.

- **Match counts race exact against estimated.** Postgres has no cheap exact count for a full-text predicate, and a true `count(*)` is a multi-second walk for broad terms. `countMatches` runs two queries in parallel: an exact count bounded to 1,000 rows with a hard `statement_timeout`, and the planner's instant row estimate. Rare terms count exactly ("515 results"). Broad or awkward multi-word queries fall back to the rounded estimate ("~34,000 results"). The whole thing is bounded to a few hundred milliseconds and streams in, so it never blocks the results.
- **[Drizzle](https://orm.drizzle.team)** for the schema and migrations, **[Tailwind v4](https://tailwindcss.com)** for styling.

See [`src/lib/queries.ts`](src/lib/queries.ts) for the query builder and [`src/app/page.tsx`](src/app/page.tsx) for the streaming boundaries.

## Deployment

Deployed on Vercel in `cle1` (Cleveland), next to the Neon compute in `us-east-2`, to keep the SQL-over-HTTP round trip short. The Neon compute is pinned (see [`neon.ts`](neon.ts)) so the first query after an idle period is not paying a cold start. The dominant cost driver is the pinned Neon compute (no scale-to-zero), not per-request query load.

Set `DATABASE_URL_UNPOOLED` to the direct Neon connection string and `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` to your Jev key (used by the on-demand judge endpoint). Env vars are baked at build time, so redeploy after changing them.

## Local dev

1. **Install and configure.**

   ```bash
   npm install
   cp .env.example .env   # fill in DATABASE_URL_UNPOOLED
   ```

2. **Create the schema and load the corpus.** The seed streams the [ClickHouse Hacker News dataset](https://clickhouse.com/docs/get-started/sample-datasets/hacker-news) straight into Postgres with parallel `COPY`, then builds the indexes. BM25 indexes are opt-in because they are large:

   ```bash
   npm run db:migrate           # extensions + tables + btree/trigram indexes
   npm run db:seed -- --bm25    # download, COPY, generated column, all indexes
   ```

   Useful seed flags: `--streams=8`, `--batch=20000`, `--limit=100000` (small sample), `--skip-download`, `--skip-unzip`.

   Getting Hacker News into the database, and keeping it current, is handled by the companion project [`rishi-raj-jain/hn-search`](https://github.com/rishi-raj-jain/hn-search): the ClickHouse seed, the two-phase [`db:backfill`](scripts/backfill.ts) that closes the late-2021-to-now gap from the [HN Firebase API](https://github.com/HackerNews/API), and an hourly Vercel cron sync that upserts the newest items. This repo shares the same `items` schema and adds the Jev judging layer on top.

3. **Run it.**

   ```bash
   npm run dev
   ```

### Scripts

| Command                          | Purpose                                                                 |
| -------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `npm run dev` / `build`          | Next.js dev server / production build                                   |
| `npm run typecheck`              | `tsc`                                                                   |
| `npm run format`                 | Prettier over the repo                                                  |
| `npm run db:generate`            | Regenerate Drizzle migrations from `src/db/schema.ts`                   |
| `npm run db:migrate`             | Apply extensions, the `items` table, and the judge/rate-limit additions |
| `npm run db:seed`                | Bulk-load the HN dump (add `--bm25` to build search indexes)            |
| `npm run db:backfill`            | Two-phase (fetch to disk, then load) backfill of the 2021-to-now gap    |
| `npm run db:judge`               | Batch-score the top threads with Jev (add `--force` to re-score)        |
| `tsx scripts/inspect-indexes.ts` | Dump table columns, extensions, and index sizes                         |

readme_preview:
# Jev Agent Tools

**Ask a short question. Use the conversation you already have.**

One TypeScript core, a native **Pi tool**, and a local **Codex MCP tool**. Agents call `jev_decide` with their current intent and typed questions. The tool collects a bounded excerpt of the correct conversation and returns compact TOON.

Uses `~typesafe/jev-latest` through OpenRouter's Decisions API. Jev returns judgments, not generated prose. It can classify failures, compare candidates against explicit criteria, or score evidence against a rubric. It does not prove mathematics, certify an architecture, or grant permission to act.

## Install

Requires **Node.js 22.19+**. Native Pi integration targets **Pi 0.85.x**. Release bundles include runtime dependencies; building is not required for use.

### Pi

```sh
pi install git:https://github.com/RobertKoval/jev-agent-tools@v0.1.0
```

Run `/reload` or start Pi. The tool and shared skill become available. The extension also works with Pi's in-memory sessions.

### Codex

```sh
git clone https://github.com/RobertKoval/jev-agent-tools.git
cd jev-agent-tools
git checkout v0.1.0
codex mcp add jev -- node "$PWD/dist/cli.mjs" mcp
```

Start a new Codex task. Optionally link this checkout's `skills/jev` into `~/.agents/skills/jev` if that location is unused. The repository also contains a Codex plugin manifest bundling the skill and MCP configuration.

For environment-only credentials, add `env_vars = ["OPENROUTER_API_KEY", "PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR"]` inside `[mcp_servers.jev]` in your Codex configuration so the server receives those variables. Do not store the key itself in that configuration. The bundled plugin already declares forwarding.

Codex must supply the concrete thread ID in MCP metadata, and its persisted session files must be accessible on the server's host. This targets local Codex; ephemeral Codex sessions and hosted web chats without local logs are unsupported. Missing or ambiguous context fails explicitly.

## Authentication and data

Set `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`, or configure OpenRouter in Pi. The native extension uses Pi's provider auth API. Codex and the CLI can read an API key from `~/.pi/agent/auth.json` (or `$PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR/auth.json`). Never put keys into tool arguments.

Every invocation sends the selected conversation and tool excerpts to **OpenRouter/TypeSafe**. This tool does not crawl project files, save transcript copies, cache responses, or automatically retry requests. It does not guarantee provider-side caching or data-retention policies.

## Agent interface

`intent` describes what the agent is doing now: 1–2 sentences, at most 600 Unicode characters. Do not repeat historical results in it or in the questions. Context is automatic and mandatory.

```json
{
  "intent": "I am classifying the latest test failure before choosing a fix",
  "questions": {
    "cause": {
      "type": "choice",
      "instructions": "Which cause is supported by the latest test output?",
      "criteria": {
        "configuration": "Missing or invalid configuration",
        "implementation": "Incorrect program behavior",
        "unknown": "The evidence does not distinguish these causes"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Question types: `noul` returns the probability of yes; `choice` selects among 2–255 named options; `score` evaluates 2–10 ordered descriptive levels. Instructions and descriptions are text strings. Independent questions can share one request; each sees the same context but not other questions or answers.

Output contains only answers, confidence where provided, and full probability distributions in TOON. Scores start at zero and may be fractional. Confidence is not proof; validate consequential conclusions against primary evidence.

## Context selection

- Pi follows the active ancestry, excludes sibling branches, and respects encountered compaction boundaries. Harness summaries are labeled.
- Codex selects the exact thread's rollout, replays compaction replacements and rollbacks, and never picks another task's most recently modified log.
- Defaults: 100 entries, up to 24,000 UTF-8 context bytes, and a 30,000-byte serialized request. **These are bytes, not tokens.** Codex reads at most an 8 MiB tail; Pi traversal is bounded too.
- The latest user or inter-agent message in the scanned window gets reserved space. Worker assignments retain sender provenance. Recent evidence fills the remaining budget in chronological order. Tool output is capped at 2,000 bytes per block with a short associated call when available.
- Reasoning, harness boilerplate, duplicated events and prior Jev tool results are excluded. Incomplete final JSONL writes are skipped.

This is a bounded excerpt, not a complete history or semantic retrieval system. Omitted evidence may matter. More context does not necessarily improve Jev's judgments.

## CLI

The same core supports Codex shell calls and diagnostics:

```sh
node dist/cli.mjs choose 'Which cause does the latest output support?' \
  --intent 'I am diagnosing the failed check' \
  -o configuration='Invalid configuration' \
  -o implementation='Incorrect behavior' \
  -o unknown='Insufficient evidence'
```

`CODEX_THREAD_ID` selects the current task; `--session /path/to/rollout.jsonl` selects an explicit Codex log. Use `decide --questions @questions.json` for several questions, or `--questions -` for stdin. Manual state/context flags are not supported.

`--dry-run` prints the request **including selected logs** without credentials or network. `--debug-json` returns full diagnostics. Keep both out of routine agent output. Run `node dist/cli.mjs --help` for selection controls.

## Development

```sh
npm ci --ignore-scripts
npm run check
```

Release bundles in `dist/` are committed and regenerated by `npm run build`. Tests cover validation, context isolation, compaction, bounded large-log reads, transport behavior and output preservation. Live checks require an OpenRouter key and installed harnesses.

Run `node scripts/live-check.mjs pi codex` for an explicit **paid** acceptance test using your configured harness providers and Jev. It asks the same question in two separate conversations with different selected animals, checks the actual tool results, and prints only a compact outcome. Codex persists its test conversation through its normal session logging.

MIT, Robert Koval and contributors. See `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` for bundled dependencies.

[Jev limitations](https://docs.typesafe.ai/model-jaggedness/jev-1.13) · [Pi extensions](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/main/packages/coding-agent/docs/extensions.md) · [OpenRouter Decisions API](https://openrouter.ai/docs/api/api-reference/alphadecisions/submit-a-decisions-questions-and-answers-request)

# tierjev

Tier lists ranked by [Jev](https://vercel.com/ai-gateway/models/jev), TypeSafe AI's classifier, through Vercel AI Gateway.

## Run

```bash
cp .env.example .env   # add AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY
bun install
bun dev
```

Next.js App Router. The classifier lives in `src/app/api/classify/route.ts`; payment endpoints go next to it.

## Deploy

1. Import the repo on Vercel. Next.js is detected automatically. The main page is prerendered static and served from the CDN; only `/api/classify` runs as a function.
2. Set `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY` in the project's environment variables.
3. Add Upstash Redis from the Vercel Marketplace (Storage tab). It injects `KV_REST_API_URL` and `KV_REST_API_TOKEN`. Without it the app still works but nothing is cached or rate limited.

## How ranking works

One request per set. The whole item list is the shared `state`; each item gets a `score` question with the rubric F, D, C, B, A, S. The tier is the rung with the highest probability, the score orders items within a tier, and the probability is shown as confidence on hover.

## Sharing

`POST /api/share` stores the list in Redis under an 8-character id. `/s/<id>` renders once, then Vercel serves the cached page from the CDN. Its social image at `/s/<id>/og` is generated with `next/og` and cached at the edge for a year. Shared pages never call Jev.

## Manual sorting

Tiles become draggable when the rate limit kicks in or after the Customize link in the footer. Manual moves drop the Jev confidence for that tile.

## Cache and limits

- Rankings are cached in Redis for 24 hours, keyed by a hash of the normalised criterion and the sorted item names. Cache hits never reach Jev and do not count against the rate limit.
- 40 items per request, 30 uncached rankings and 20 shares per IP per hour, counted in Redis so the limit holds across function instances. A 429 carries `Retry-After`, and the UI locks the Rank button with a countdown.
- Budget: a cache miss costs about four Redis commands, a hit one. The Upstash free tier covers 500K commands a month.

## Next

- Pre-generated sets with images stored in a database (`Item.image` is already rendered when present).
- Jev-powered search over the set catalogue.

# template-oss

Template for open-source TypeScript projects: a pnpm + Turborepo monorepo with a publishable
package, an Astro Starlight docs site, and a CI pipeline that spends free public-repo minutes on
breadth.

## What is in it

| Piece              | Details                                                                                                                                                    |
| ------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `packages/example` | Publishable ESM package built with tsdown; publint + attw + a pack smoke test                                                                              |
| `packages/config`  | Shared tsdown preset (`@rxova/config/tsdown.base`), the one home of the build defaults                                                                     |
| `packages/tooling` | `verify` (the pre-push gate), changeset gate, release-commit detection, pack smoke                                                                         |
| `apps/docs`        | Astro Starlight, links validator, sitemap, deployed to GitHub Pages                                                                                        |
| Quality            | TypeScript 6 strict, ESLint 10 + typescript-eslint, Prettier, Vitest 5 (95%/file), knip (unused files/exports/deps), sherif (one version per dep)          |
| Hooks              | Husky: lint-staged + typecheck + tests on commit, commitlint, `verify` on push                                                                             |
| Releases           | Changesets → version PR → npm with trusted publishing and provenance                                                                                       |
| CI                 | Parallel jobs; tests on Node 22/24 × Linux/macOS/Windows; CodeQL; Codecov; one `all checks` gate                                                           |
| Renovate           | Weekly, grouped PRs labelled `skip-changeset`; patch/minor updates and lockfile maintenance auto-merge once `all checks` passes (`.github/renovate.json5`) |

## After creating a repository from this template

1. Replace the template's name everywhere, and rename the example package:
   ```sh
   grep -rl template-oss --exclude-dir=node_modules --exclude-dir=.git . | xargs sed -i '' 's/template-oss/<repo>/g'
   git mv packages/example packages/<name>   # then update "name" and "repository.directory"
   ```
2. `pnpm install`
3. Create the labels Renovate and the changeset gate use (templates do not copy labels):
   ```sh
   gh label create dependencies --color 0366d6 && gh label create skip-changeset --color ededed
   ```
4. **Docs:** Settings → Pages → Source: **GitHub Actions**. The Docs workflow skips itself until
   then.
5. **npm:** publish the first version by hand (`npm publish --access public` in the package), add a
   trusted publisher on npmjs.com (repository `rxova/<repo>`, workflow `release.yml`), then set the
   repository variable `RELEASE_ENABLED` to `true`. Releases stay off until you do.
6. **Branch protection** on `main`: require the `all checks` status.
7. Optional: add a `CODECOV_TOKEN` secret for coverage comments.

## Commands

```sh
pnpm install        # dependencies and git hooks
pnpm test           # unit tests, coverage enforced per file
pnpm docs           # docs dev server
pnpm run verify     # everything CI runs, in order
pnpm changeset      # record a change to a published package
```

See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for the rest.

# jevy — 自炼的 Jev 式类型化判断模型

仿照 [Laya](https://huggingface.co/convaiinnovations/laya-typed-decisions) 的思路，
在一张 **GTX 1650（4GB 显存）** 上微调出的 **Jev 式类型化决策模型**（118M 参数，中英文）。

> [Jev](https://typesafe.ai) 是 TypeSafe AI 的 "System One" 模型：输入状态 + 类型化问题，
> 输出**带概率的决策**而非生成文本。jevy 是它的开源平替之一——用官方 Jev API 当老师
> 蒸馏而来，专做**意图识别 / 候选择优**这类判断任务。

- **单次前向**输出所有候选的概率分布，零自回归解码
- **候选数量推理时随意变**——加新意图不用重训
- **4GB 显存可训**：全量重训约 10 分钟；数据、训练脚本、评测集全部开源

## 目录

- [对比结果](#对比结果)
- [快速开始](#快速开始)
- [API](#api)
- [自己训一个](#自己训一个)
- [训练数据](#训练数据)
- [实现细节](#实现细节)
- [已知边界](#已知边界)

## 对比结果

所有数字均为实测（硬件：GTX 1650 4GB；老师：官方 `jev-1.13.0`）。

### 1) 与官方 Jev 的判断一致率（合成意图域，6 条 held-out 消息）

| 模型 | 一致率 | 备注 |
|---|---|---|
| NanoJev（0.6B，游戏域） | 33% | 领域不匹配 |
| Laya（421M，客服域） | 83% | 唯一分歧：发票导出判 billing（老师判 other） |
| **jevy（118M，本仓库）** | **100%** | 训练数据 771 条蒸馏样本 |

### 2) jevy 内部两轮迭代（dev 一致率，混合域）

| 版本 | 蒸馏数据 | dev 一致率 | held-out |
|---|---|---|---|
| v1 | 271 条模板消息 | 87%（54 条 dev） | 5/6 |
| v2 | 771 条（+500 模板、难例过采样） | **92%（154 条 dev）** | **6/6** |

### 3) 真实工单域（公开数据集真实工单，10 类意图，40 条从未参与训练）

| 模型 | 与官方一致率 |
|---|---|
| jevy v2（仅 260 条真实样本训练） | 35%（随机基线 10%） |

诚实说明：真实文本的多样性远超模板，35% 是第一版真实域成绩，
继续扩充真实标注量是最有效的提升路径（数据集里还有 1.5 万条可标）。

### 4) 常识陷阱题：*"洗车店离这里 50 米，开车去还是走路去洗车？"*

正确答案：**开车**——要去洗的是车。

| 模型 | 判断 | 分布 |
|---|---|---|
| Laya | ✅ 开车 | 66% / 34% |
| jevy | ✅ 开车 | 63% / 37% |
| 官方 jev-1.13.0（英文转译输入） | ⚠️ 走路 | walk 83% / drive 41% |

### 5) 实测发现：官方 API 拒绝中文输入

`api.typesafe.ai` 的网关对非 ASCII 内容直接返回 403（key 有效性与此无关，
同请求换英文即 200）。中文场景请翻译后调用官方，或直接用本地后端。

## 快速开始

```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt
```

### 方式 A：下载训练好的权重（GitHub Releases）

从 [Releases](../../releases) 下载 `jevy-model.zip`，解压为 `model/`，然后：

```bash
python intent_server.py --model-dir model --port 8767
```

### 方式 B：自己训（约 10 分钟，4GB 显存即可）

训练数据已包含在本仓库 `data/`，直接复现：

```bash
python train_intent.py \
    --data data/train_synthetic_v2.jsonl data/train_synthetic_v3.jsonl \
           data/train_synthetic_v4.jsonl data/train_real.jsonl \
    --out model
python intent_server.py --model-dir model --port 8767
```

## API

与 NanoJev / Laya 服务器同契约（`POST /api/v1/decide`）：

```bash
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8767/api/v1/decide \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "{\"state\": \"我的手机充不进电，买了才两周。\", \
       \"questions\": {\"intent\": {\"type\": \"choice\", \
         \"instructions\": \"判断用户消息最符合哪个意图\", \
         \"criteria\": {\"hardware\": \"硬件故障\", \"billing\": \"账单问题\", \"other\": \"其他\"}}}}"
```

返回：

```json
{"object": "decision", "model": "jev-distill-student",
 "decisions": {"intent": {"type": "choice", "value": "hardware",
   "probabilities": {"hardware": 0.55, "other": 0.15, "billing": 0.02, ...},
   "confidence": 0.55}}}
```

也支持批量（`{"states": [{"id", "state", "questions"}, ...]}`，单请求最多 128 条）。
Python 调用见 [`examples/intent.py`](examples/intent.py)。

注意：候选 `criteria` 的数量与内容**推理时随意指定**，无需重训——
这是标记位架构的直接好处。

## 自己训一个

三步，全部脚本化：

```bash
# 1. 写你的意图集和消息清单（UTF-8，每行一条）
#    data/intents_synthetic.json: {"weather": "查天气", "music": "播放音乐", ...}

# 2. 官方 Jev 当老师打软标签（需要 TYPESAFE_API_KEY；中文需先转英文，见上文发现）
python collect_distill.py --messages-file msgs.txt \
    --intents-file data/intents_synthetic.json \
    --api-key $TYPESAFE_API_KEY --out data/train_mine.jsonl

# 3. 蒸馏训练 + 温度校准，然后起服务
python train_intent.py --data data/train_mine.jsonl --out model
python intent_server.py --model-dir model --port 8767
```

数据格式（软标签蒸馏，一行一条）：

```json
{"id": "a11b2dcb", "message": "Where is my order #12345?",
 "intents": {"shipping": "物流问题", "...": "..."},
 "teacher": {"intent": "shipping",
             "dist": {"shipping": 0.71, "other": 0.12, "...": "..."},
             "model": "jev-1.13.0 (official)"}}
```

## 实现细节

Laya 的三个核心思路的迷你实现：

1. **编码器而非解码器**：`paraphrase-multilingual-MiniLM-L12-v2`（118M，XLM-R 系，中英通吃），
   一次前向给所有候选打分；
2. **选项标记位**：每个候选前插一个 `[OPT]` 标记 token，线性头读标记位隐状态出 logit——
   因此候选数量动态可变；
3. **软标签蒸馏 + 温度校准**：老师 noul 分布做 KL 蒸馏（比硬标签信号多），
   训后在 dev 上拟合温度修概率过冲；另带 best-dev 选点与难例过采样
   （学生与老师分歧 ×3 的样本）。

训练配置：batch 16、AdamW（头 1e-3 / 底座 3e-5）、fp16 autocast、约 1600 步，
GTX 1650 上 10~15 分钟。

## 已知边界

- 真实工单域第一版仅 35%（见对比结果 3），扩充真实标注量是当前最有效的提升路径
- 底座只测到 118M：278M mpnet + Adafactor 在 4GB 卡上 fp16 数值不稳（dev 掉到 47% 已回退），
  更大底座建议冻结底层或用 8-bit 优化器
- 只实现了 `choice` 类型；`score` / `noul`（布尔）问题会明确报 400
- 官方 API 计费按 token，标注 1000 条约 40 万 input token——注意配额

## 数据与许可

- 代码：MIT
- `data/train_real.jsonl` / `data/test_real.jsonl` 来自公开数据集
  [Tobi-Bueck/customer-support-tickets](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Tobi-Bueck/customer-support-tickets)
  （CC BY-NC 4.0），**仅限非商业用途**；合成消息与老师标注为本项目生成
- 感谢 TypeSafe AI 的 Jev 与开源平替社区（[awesome-jev](https://github.com/yibie/awesome-jev)、
  NanoJev、Laya）提供的思路与对照

readme_preview:
# Phishing triage: TypeSafe Jev 1.13 vs GPT-5.6 Luna

A small, reproducible test: can a specialised classification model triage phishing emails as well as a general-purpose chat model, and what does each cost in time and money?

![Jev vs Luna, final frame](media/jev_vs_luna.png)

🎥 Videos (replay of every decision, email by email): [jev_vs_luna.mp4](media/jev_vs_luna.mp4) · [jev_replay.mp4](media/jev_replay.mp4)

## Results

100 labelled emails (50 phishing, 50 safe). Same emails and same instructions for both models, decision threshold 50%.

| | TypeSafe Jev 1.13 | GPT-5.6 Luna |
|---|---|---|
| Accuracy | **81%** | 78% |
| Phishing caught (recall) | **33 / 50** (66%) | 29 / 50 (58%) |
| False alarms | 2 / 50 (4%) | **1 / 50** (2%) |
| Time per email, median | **0.42 s** | 2.63 s |
| Cost per email | **$0.000037** | $0.000155 |
| Cost per 1,000 emails | **$0.04** | $0.16 |
| Cost for the full run | $0.0037 | $0.0155 |

**Reading it:**

- **Accuracy is a tie.** 81% vs 78% is a difference of 3 emails out of 100, which is within what random sampling alone can produce.
- **Speed and cost are not close.** Jev is about 6× faster and 4× cheaper per email.
- **Both models miss about 1 in 3 phishing emails at the 50% threshold.** Neither is a standalone filter. Both are better suited to a triage layer.

## Method

1. **Data.** [`zefang-liu/phishing-email-dataset`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/zefang-liu/phishing-email-dataset) on Hugging Face (about 18.6k emails, labelled `Phishing Email` / `Safe Email`). Empty texts are dropped, then a balanced sample of 50 per class is drawn with a fixed seed (`random_state=42`), so every model sees the exact same 100 emails.
2. **No label leakage.** Only the `Email Text` column is sent to a model. The label stays local and is used only for scoring afterwards.
3. **Same question for both models:**
   > Is this email a phishing attempt?
   > Phishing: Tries to trick the reader into giving credentials, money, or clicking malicious links.
   > Not phishing: Legitimate email with no deceptive intent.
4. **Models (via [OpenRouter](https://openrouter.ai)):**
   - `typesafe/jev-1.13` (served as `jev-1.13-20260917`) through the Decisions API, as a `noul` question. A noul is a yes/no answer returned as a probability from 0 to 1.
   - `openai/gpt-5.6-luna` through Chat Completions, asked for "the probability (0 to 1) that the email is phishing", with a strict JSON schema for the answer. Default settings, `max_tokens=1000`.
5. **Scoring.** A probability above 0.5 counts as a "phishing" prediction. We compare predictions with the labels to get accuracy, recall and the false-positive rate.
6. **Time and cost.** Time is the full request round-trip measured from the client, per email. Cost is what OpenRouter reported for each request. Listed prices: Jev $0.042/M input tokens and $0.00/M output tokens; Luna $0.20/M input tokens and $1.20/M output tokens.
7. **Rate limits.** When the API returns HTTP 429 (rate limited), the request is retried with increasing waits (2 s, 5 s, 10 s, 20 s, 40 s). Only the attempt that succeeds is timed, so the waits and rejected attempts don't count against a model's speed.

## An important caveat: two kinds of "probability"

The dots in the charts are each model's probability, but the two models produce them differently:

- **Jev** returns a probability by design. That's the whole point of its `noul` answer type, and its answers spread out smoothly (50 distinct values across 100 emails).
- **Luna** writes its probability as text. Like most chat models, the number it writes isn't calibrated: 86 of its 100 answers are ≤ 0.03 or ≥ 0.97 (Jev: 27), and "0.01" (34 of 100) really means "I'm sure it's safe".

This does **not** affect accuracy, recall or false alarms, which only depend on which side of 50% an answer falls. It **does** mean the charts shouldn't be read as two equally calibrated confidence scores. What they do show is how each model behaves when it's wrong: Luna's misses sit near 0% (confidently wrong), while Jev's sit in the uncertain middle, where a human-review rule could catch them.

A like-for-like comparison of confidence would use Luna's token probabilities (logprobs) instead of its stated number. That's left for a follow-up.

## Limitations

- 100 emails, one dataset, one run per model. This is a pilot, not a benchmark.
- The dataset is older, public email (a lot of it is spam and mailing-list traffic). Modern targeted phishing looks different.
- The threshold is fixed at 50%. No tuning, no ROC AUC yet.
- Time depends on network conditions and provider load at the time of the run (21 September 2026).

## Repository layout

```
src/phishing_eval.py      run one model on the 100 emails -> results/results_<model>.csv
src/animate_results.py    replay the results as videos + final-frame PNGs -> media/
results/                  raw per-email results (probability, prediction, time, tokens, cost)
media/                    videos and still images
```

## Reproduce

Requires Python 3.10+, `ffmpeg` (for the videos) and an [OpenRouter API key](https://openrouter.ai/keys).

```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt
cp .env.example .env                 # then put your key in .env

python src/phishing_eval.py jev      # about $0.004
python src/phishing_eval.py luna     # about $0.02
python src/animate_results.py        # free, re-renders media/ from results/
```

In the videos, email snippets are cleaned of leftover HTML and CSS code, and sexually explicit spam is shown as "[explicit spam, text hidden]". Those emails still count in the results.

## License

Code: MIT, see [LICENSE](LICENSE).

Data: the email texts in `results/` come from [`zefang-liu/phishing-email-dataset`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/zefang-liu/phishing-email-dataset), licensed under LGPL-3.0. The dataset includes real spam and phishing content.

# OpenJEV adaptive medical triage

Testbed for TypeSafe's Jev (via the OpenJEV proxy) as a **calibrated decision
layer** for clinical history-taking.

    POST https://api.openjev.sh/v1/systemone

Not a diagnostic tool. Every run ends in a handoff to a clinician, and the
model itself agrees: `safe_to_act_without_clinician` came back 0.03-0.04 in
every single state tested, including the ones it was 100% certain about.

**Live demo:** https://ts0047.github.io/jev-triage-demo/

## Files

    .env                  API keys, chmod 600, git-ignored (see .env.example)
    state_a.txt           day-5 tropical fever, no vitals, nothing tested (underdetermined)
    state_b.txt           same patient + NS1 positive, platelets 62k falling (dengue, decisive)
    state_c.txt           same symptoms, NS1 NEGATIVE, vivax on smear (contradicts the anchor)
    state_d.txt           lupus presentation -- deliberately OUTSIDE the differential
    questions.json        9-question battery, all three primitives
    run_test.py           single-shot: run the battery against one state
    findings_bank.json    25 history findings with per-disease likelihoods
    triage_loop.py        adaptive multi-round history-taking loop
    docs/                 static web demo (see Web demo below)

## Single-shot results

                                  state_a          state_b          state_c
    primary_diagnosis             dengue 0.63      dengue 1.00      malaria 1.00
    evidence_sufficient           0.04  no         0.75  yes        0.66  yes
    diagnostic_certainty          1.74 / 3         3.00 / 3         3.00 / 3
    most_useful_next_test         dengue_ns1       none_needed      none_needed
    warning_signs_present         0.21             0.96             0.43
    care_urgency                  1.97             2.91             2.48 (conf 0.48)
    safe_without_clinician        0.03             0.03             0.04

Two findings worth keeping:

- **Diagnosis and sufficiency decouple.** On state_a it leaned dengue at 0.68
  while simultaneously saying "evidence not sufficient" at 0.04. A leading
  hypothesis plus an explicit refusal to act on it.
- **It drops the anchor.** state_c has a symptom block byte-identical to
  state_b's, but NS1 negative + positive smear moved dengue to 0.000 and
  malaria to 1.000.

## Why a flat bank, not a decision tree

A tree hardcodes question order at authoring time. Jev gives you a live
posterior after every turn, so the best next question is whichever most splits
the *current* differential -- computable, not authorable. Trees also explode
combinatorially, have no node for "I don't know", and collapse a calibrated
0.68 into a binary branch, discarding the thing you're paying for.

## Loop architecture

    1. Jev scores the disease choice + one noul per unasked finding -- ONE call
    2. Python picks the finding with the highest expected information gain
    3. Phrasing layer turns it into a human sentence (template, Ollama, OpenRouter)
    4. Patient replies in free text
    5. Jev interprets the reply back into a structured fact
    6. Append to state, drop the finding, repeat

**The LLM never selects a question and never reads a reply.** It is a phrasing
layer at the edges only. Every clinical decision stays in the calibrated
component -- that is the whole point of the design.

Stop conditions (all four are needed):

    outside >= 0.60 or choice == "other"   -> escalate, bank cannot help
    max(posterior) >= 0.97                 -> dominance; needs a lab test now
    best_eig < 0.02 bits                   -> no question left worth asking
    round > cap                            -> hard ceiling (8 by default)

## Results: 25-finding bank, synthetic patients

    truth           questions  path                                          outcome
    scrub_typhus    1          eschar(+)                                     matched, 1.00
    typhoid         5          eschar- scrub- cough- stepladder+ water+      matched, 0.92
    leptospirosis   8          ...flood_water+ then confirmatory sweep       matched, 0.84
    lupus (state_d) 0          -- outside=0.95 on round 1                    escalated

Question ordering is genuinely evidence-driven: round 1 always opens with
`eschar` (0.185 bits, the single best splitter of this differential), but the
paths diverge immediately based on the answer. In the typhoid run,
`untreated_water` jumped to 0.352 bits at round 5 -- *after* stepladder fever
landed -- because confirming the exposure route only pays off once the disease
is plausible. Nothing in the bank encodes that ordering.

Cost: $0.0003 - $0.001 per full consultation, ~1.5s per round.

## Three bugs found and fixed during testing

1. **Saturation kills EIG.** Jev reports choice probabilities as exactly 1.00 /
   0.00. Entropy collapses to zero, every expected-gain score becomes 0.000,
   and the loop picks questions in arbitrary bank order -- it asked 5 useless
   questions after already being certain. Fixed with `temper()`, a 2% uniform
   floor. The saturation is an artefact of the *reported* distribution, not
   real certainty, so flooring it is the honest correction.
2. **`evidence_sufficient` never fires.** It stayed at 0.04-0.10 even at 100%
   posterior, because history alone genuinely cannot confirm a tropical fever --
   it wants a lab test, and no amount of questioning will produce one. Stopping
   on that alone loops forever. Added `--dominance` (posterior >= 0.97) and
   `--min-gain` (best question worth < 0.02 bits) as the real terminators.
3. **A closed option set produces confident wrong answers.** With six diseases
   and no escape hatch, the lupus state (`state_d.txt`) was answered
   **"dengue 0.42"** after three wasted rounds. Given an `other` option and an
   `outside_differential` noul, the same input returned **"other" at 1.00** and
   escalated on round one. Widening the disease list is the *second* fix; the
   escape hatch is the first, and it is what makes the system safe at any bank
   size.

The second one is the more interesting result: the model was right and the loop
design was wrong. `evidence_sufficient` is not a "stop asking" signal, it is a
"stop and order a test" signal.

## Web demo

Three static pages, no build step, no framework:

    docs/index.html        case studies -- pre-generated run transcripts
    docs/live.html         live consultation -- user types symptoms, loop runs in-browser
    docs/coverage.html     the six illnesses, discrimination matrix, what falls outside
    docs/live.js           the loop ported to client-side JS
    docs/data/*.json       transcripts + findings bank + disease notes
    docs/404.html          error page
    docs/.nojekyll         disables Jekyll on GitHub Pages

Serve locally:

    cd docs && python3 -m http.server 8777

### Case studies (`index.html`)

Fetches `data/*.json` at runtime and renders everything from it: verdict, final
differential, per-round question selection with the full candidate ranking, the
25-finding bank (asked findings highlighted), and measured cost. Regenerate the
data and the page updates -- nothing is hardcoded in the HTML.

    python3 triage_loop.py state_a.txt --rounds 8 --truth typhoid \
        --phraser openrouter --json docs/data/typhoid.json

### Live consultation (`live.html`)

The whole loop ported to JS, calling `api.openjev.sh` directly from the browser
(CORS is open -- verified). Users describe symptoms in plain language and answer
the questions the model chooses.

Deliberate design decisions:

- **A demo key is embedded in `live.js`** so visitors need no setup. It is
  public by construction on a static host -- anyone can read it in devtools.
  Rotate at openjev.sh if abused. A visitor-supplied key (Advanced disclosure)
  overrides it and is kept in `sessionStorage` only.
- **No phrasing LLM client-side.** Probes render verbatim, so no model rewords
  a clinical question unsupervised and no second credential is needed.
- **Consent gate** before the form; nothing identifying should be entered.
- **`red_flags` noul checked every round**, short-circuiting before any question
  is asked. Verified: breathless + confused + bleeding returned urgency 3.00/3
  with zero questions and routed straight to emergency care.

Known quirk: free-text intake is more suggestive than a structured state file.
The same case pushed the top outcome to 0.95 on round 1 versus 0.66 as
`state_a.txt`, so the live tab often hits dominance before asking much. Raise
`LIMITS.dominance` in `live.js` if you want it to work harder before conceding.

### Coverage (`coverage.html`)

Per-illness cards (vector, incubation, clinical picture, deterioration signs,
confirmatory test) with the findings that point to each, a 25x6 discrimination
matrix, and an explicit account of what falls outside the differential and what
happens then.

### Hosting

`docs/` is a static directory with no build step and no server-side code. It
works as-is on GitHub Pages (Settings -> Pages -> main branch, /docs folder),
Netlify, Vercel, Cloudflare Pages, or any static host.

`index.html` and `coverage.html` make no API calls at all. `live.html` calls
OpenJEV from the browser with the embedded demo key. If that key gets abused,
the fix that keeps zero-setup UX is a small Cloudflare Worker proxying the API
with the key server-side.

### Adding a case to the demo

1. Write a new `state_*.txt`.
2. Run the loop with `--json docs/data/<name>.json`.
3. Add `{file:'<name>.json', label:'...'}` to the `CASES` array in
   `docs/index.html`.

### Adding an illness

1. Add it to `diseases` in `findings_bank.json`.
2. Add `supports`/`against` entries on the findings that discriminate it.
3. Add a blurb to `docs/data/disease_notes.json` (used by the coverage page).
4. Copy the bank into `docs/data/findings_bank.json` -- the live and coverage
   pages read that copy.

## Usage

    python3 run_test.py state_c.txt

    python3 triage_loop.py state_a.txt --rounds 8 --truth leptospirosis
    python3 triage_loop.py state_a.txt --rounds 8 --phraser ollama --model qwen2.5:3b
    python3 triage_loop.py state_a.txt --rounds 8 --phraser openrouter
    python3 triage_loop.py state_d.txt --rounds 6            # escalation path

`--truth` drives a SYNTHETIC patient that answers from a hidden profile. It
exists to observe question-selection behaviour and measures nothing about real
diagnostic accuracy.

### Setup

    cp .env.example .env && chmod 600 .env
    # fill in OPENJEV_API_KEY (https://openjev.sh)
    # optional: OPENROUTER_API_KEY for --phraser openrouter

## Known limits

- The findings bank is hand-authored and its likelihoods are plausible, not
  sourced from epidemiological data. Real use needs real priors.
- Six diseases, one clinical presentation (tropical fever). Anything else must
  hit the escape hatch -- which is tested, but the list is still narrow.
- `warning_signs_present` scored only 0.43 on the malaria state because the
  criteria wording listed dengue-flavoured danger signs. Prompt-design fault,
  not a model fault -- make warning-sign criteria disease-agnostic.
- Findings are treated as conditionally independent in the Bayes update. They
  are not (rash and petechiae correlate). Fine for ranking, wrong for
  reporting a true posterior.
- The embedded demo key in `live.js` is public and in git history permanently.

## Not a medical device

This is a research demonstration of calibrated decision-model architecture. It
provides no medical advice, is not validated for clinical use, and must not be
used to diagnose or treat any person. See LICENSE.

readme_preview:
# awesome-jev-compaction

**Using [Jev](https://docs.typesafe.ai) to manage an agent's memory and keep its context small.**

[![Tool output arrives, Jev scores every segment, the low-value parts move out to a store](docs/gate.gif)](docs/index.html)

That's [`docs/index.html`](docs/index.html) — open it to drive it yourself.
[`docs/showcase.html`](docs/showcase.html) has the numbers behind it, with a threshold
slider you can drag.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Waxmell114514/awesome-jev-compaction
cd awesome-jev-compaction
uv venv .venv && uv pip install --python .venv/bin/python -e '.[dev]'
.venv/bin/python demo.py      # runs offline, no API key needed
```

---

## The problem

An agent's context fills up. The usual fix is **compaction**: when it gets too long, ask a
model to summarise the old parts and replace them.

Two things go wrong. First, rewriting the middle of the context **breaks the prompt cache**,
so every later turn pays full price again. Second, a summary is *generated* text — the model
can quietly invent a detail, and now that invented detail is your agent's memory.

---

## Our idea

Three parts. Each one is simple on its own.

### 1. Filter at the door

Split the context into two pieces: a **frozen part** at the front, and a **work area** at the
end. The frozen part only ever grows — nothing in it is ever rewritten. So the cache over it
never breaks.

New tool output goes into the work area. Before it goes in, ask Jev whether it's worth
keeping. Low-scoring parts never enter.

### 2. Move it out and don't delete it

What the gate removes doesn't disappear. It goes into a store, and leaves one line behind:

```
[[elided id=r:8506e122 lines=1-21 tokens=364 "npm http fetch GET 200 https://registry..."]]
```

The agent gets an `expand` tool. If it needs what's behind that line, it asks for it and gets
the **original text, byte for byte**. So a wrong decision costs one extra round trip — not
lost information.

Because Jev can't write text, what you keep is always the original lines. Nothing in memory
was ever made up.

### 3. Record every decision, so you can tune it later

Every decision is logged with its score. When the agent later calls `expand` on something you
removed, that's **proof the filter was too aggressive** — it went looking for exactly what you
took away.

Later, replay the log at a different threshold. No re-running the agent, no extra Jev calls:

```
  threshold    kept   relocated   tokens saved   still missed
  0.10           12           3          1,092              0
  0.35            9           6          1,260              3
```

`0.10` saves 1,092 tokens and takes away nothing the agent came back for. `0.35` saves 168
more tokens and costs three. Now you can choose.

---

## Using the repo

Start with the demo. It runs offline against a scripted stand-in, so you don't need a key:

```bash
.venv/bin/python demo.py                            # six short acts
TYPESAFE_API_KEY=sk-... .venv/bin/python demo.py    # same code, real Jev
```

### Connecting a real key

Set `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` and everything switches to real Jev — `demo.py` picks it up, and
`HttpJevClient()` reads it by default. To check the key actually works before wiring it into
an agent:

```bash
export TYPESAFE_API_KEY=...
.venv/bin/python -m jevctx.check
```

That makes real requests and checks three things: all three question types come back and
parse, the gate actually relocates something from a real tool output, and the pointer expands
back byte for byte. It prints latency, token usage and cost, and on failure it tells you
which of the three broke — a bad key, a malformed request, or an unreachable server.

Then read these, in this order

| File | What's in it |
|---|---|
| [`demo.py`](demo.py) | The tour. Start here. |
| `jevctx/pipeline.py` | `admit()` / `retrieve()` / `expand()` — the ~200 lines that matter |
| `jevctx/scorer.py` | How 32 questions get packed into one request |
| `jevctx/context.py` | The frozen-prefix buffer |
| `jevctx/segments.py` | Splitting output without breaking it |

To use it in your own agent

```python
from jevctx import admit, expand, InMemoryStore, ShadowLog, HttpJevClient, Origin, GateConfig

store, log, client = InMemoryStore(), ShadowLog("shadow.jsonl"), HttpJevClient()

result = admit(tool_output, Origin(source="tool:bash", ref="npm install", turn=1),
               task_digest="What the agent is currently doing.",
               turn=1, client=client, store=store, log=log,
               config=GateConfig(shadow_only=True))   # start here

# result.text goes into your context. Register `expand` as a tool.
```

**Start with `shadow_only=True`.** It scores and logs everything but changes nothing. Run it
for a day, replay the log to pick a threshold, then turn it on. Turning a context filter
straight on is how you lose a week to "the agent got worse and nobody knows when."

---

## What's not built

- Jev-driven commit points — asking "is this subtask finished?"
- Multi-dimensional labelling — type, lifetime, entities, in one call of ~15 questions
- Supersession chains — does this new record replace that old one?
- Bayesian threshold calibration — combine Jev's score with observed hit counts

# Spark Jev Email Triage

TanStack Start app with React, Vite, and strict TypeScript.

## Setup

Requires Node.js 24 and pnpm 12.5.1 (pinned in `packageManager`).

```sh
corepack enable
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
pnpm dev
```

`pnpm install` installs the Git hooks.

## Quality commands

| Command             | Purpose                                                |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `pnpm format`       | Format files with Prettier                             |
| `pnpm format:check` | Verify formatting                                      |
| `pnpm lint`         | ESLint with type-aware rules, zero warnings            |
| `pnpm typecheck`    | `tsc --noEmit` in strict mode                          |
| `pnpm test`         | Run Vitest once                                        |
| `pnpm fallow`       | Dead code, cycles, complexity, and duplication         |
| `pnpm fallow:audit` | Fallow audit of changes against `origin/main`          |
| `pnpm build`        | Production build                                       |
| `pnpm check`        | Format check, lint, typecheck, test, Fallow, and build |

Git hooks:

- `pre-commit`: lint-staged runs Prettier and ESLint on staged files.
- `commit-msg`: commitlint enforces Conventional Commits.

## Safety status

- No product features, persistence, email access, or external services.
- No secrets or deployment configuration.
- CI runs every quality command and the build on pull requests and `main`.
- On pull requests, CI also runs commitlint and the Fallow changed-code audit.
- CI fails on `git diff --check` errors or uncommitted generated files.
- Branch protection is not configured yet, so CI results are not enforced on merge.

readme_preview:
Jev Issue Labeler

Zero-config AI issue labeling

Asks [Jev](https://docs.typesafe.ai) one yes/no question per repository label, built from the description the label already has in GitHub, and adds the labels that clear a threshold. Jev returns probabilities, never text. A hostile issue body can at worst earn a wrong label: there is no comment to hijack and no tool to call. ## Quick start 1. Get an API key from [TypeSafe](https://docs.typesafe.ai) and store it as a repository secret: ```sh gh secret set TYPESAFE_API_KEY ``` This prompts for the value. If the key is already in an environment variable, pipe it in instead: ```sh printenv TYPESAFE_API_KEY | gh secret set TYPESAFE_API_KEY ``` 2. Add `.github/workflows/label-issues.yml`: ```yaml name: Label issues on: issues: types: [opened] permissions: {} jobs: label: runs-on: ubuntu-latest permissions: issues: write steps: - uses: yamadashy/jev-labeler-action@v0 with: api-key: ${{ secrets.TYPESAFE_API_KEY }} ``` The next issue gets every label whose probability is `0.8` or higher. The run's **Job Summary** lists the probability of each label considered. Add `dry-run: true` to see those numbers without touching the issue. ## Better labels **The label description is the prompt.** Improving a description on GitHub improves the labeling, and a label with no description is skipped. Some of GitHub's default descriptions mislead when read literally. `question` says *"Further information is requested"*, which describes a maintainer asking, so it never fires. Override it with `criteria`: ```yaml - uses: yamadashy/jev-labeler-action@v0 with: api-key: ${{ secrets.TYPESAFE_API_KEY }} criteria: | question: >- The author is asking how to do something with the tool, or asking the maintainers to clarify existing behaviour, rather than reporting a defect or requesting a change. ``` On [Repomix #303](https://github.com/yamadashy/repomix/issues/303) that one entry moved `question` from `0.60` to `0.88`. Exclude labels that record a decision or an event rather than a property of the text: `duplicate`, `good first issue`, `needs more information`, `triage`, `released`. ## Inputs | Input | Default | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | `api-key` | *(required)* | TypeSafe API key. | | `github-token` | `${{ github.token }}` | Needs `issues: write`. | | `threshold` | `0.8` | Apply a label at or above this probability. | | `labels` | *(all described labels)* | Allowlist, newline- or comma-separated. | | `exclude-labels` | `duplicate`, `invalid`, `wontfix`, `good first issue`, `help wanted` | Labels never to apply. | | `criteria` | *(none)* | YAML map of label to a plain-language condition, replacing its description. | | `fallback-label` | *(none)* | Applied when nothing clears the threshold. | | `skip-bots` | `true` | Skip issues opened by bots. | | `dry-run` | `false` | Write the summary, apply nothing. | | `model` | `jev-1.13.0` | Pinned so a tuned threshold does not shift when `jev-latest` moves. | | `max-body-chars` | `6000` | Longer issue bodies are truncated. | ### Customized example ```yaml - uses: yamadashy/jev-labeler-action@v0 with: api-key: ${{ secrets.TYPESAFE_API_KEY }} # Stricter than the default 0.8: fewer labels, fewer mistakes. threshold: 0.9 # Consider only these labels instead of every described label. labels: | bug enhancement question # Or keep every label and leave some out. Replaces the default list. # exclude-labels: | # duplicate # wontfix # dependencies # Your own words instead of the label's GitHub description. # A label listed here is considered even if it has no description. criteria: | bug: The author reports that the tool crashes, errors, or produces wrong output. question: The author asks how to do something rather than reporting a defect. # Applied when no label reaches the threshold. fallback-label: triage ``` ## Outputs | Output | Description | | --- | --- | | `labels` | JSON array of the labels applied (or that would be, in a dry run). | | `probabilities` | JSON object of label to probability. | | `model` | The model version that answered. | ## Security - Jev's whole reply is one number per question. Nothing in the issue can become a comment, a command, or a tool call. - The action only adds labels. It never removes, edits, closes, or comments. - The issue is read from the event payload inside the action, never through a shell. ## Measured On 270 real [Repomix](https://github.com/yamadashy/repomix) issues with `jev-1.13.0`: - 40 high-confidence picks disagreed with the existing labels. Read one by one, 38 were correct: the issue had been left unlabeled or only marked `triage`. One of the two misses was a bot-authored issue, hence `skip-bots`. - Hand-written `criteria` are stable at any threshold from `0.5` to `0.9`. Descriptions alone degrade at `0.9`. - Median 220 ms and $0.000066 per issue. All 270 cost under two cents. ## Contributing ```sh npm install npm test npm run lint npm run build # dist/ is committed; CI fails if it is stale npm run smoke -- --repo yamadashy/repomix --issue 303 # try the core on a real issue ``` ## License [MIT](./LICENSE) © Kazuki Yamada. Unofficial: not affiliated with or endorsed by TypeSafe.

readme_preview:
# jev-file-sort

`jev-file-sort` is a cross-platform file sorting CLI and Bubble Tea UI. It can classify with deterministic extension and path rules or with TypeSafe Jev.

> [!NOTE]
> This project is under development.  
> Features and behavior may change as development progresses.  
> **Features related to Jev are not yet optimized, so their accuracy may be limited.**  
> 

## Build

```sh
go build -o jev-sort ./cmd/jev-sort
```

## Usage

```sh
jev-sort config check
jev-sort run ~/Downloads --dry-run
jev-sort run ~/Downloads
jev-sort run ~/Downloads --no-confirm
jev-sort plan ~/Downloads --recursive --out plan.json
jev-sort apply plan.json
jev-sort history
jev-sort undo <run-id>
jev-sort redo <run-id>
jev-sort ui ~/Downloads
```

The UI shows operation details beside the plan on wide terminals. Use `→` or `c` to choose a category (including for entries skipped by default), `←` to go back, `m` to switch between Simple and Jev modes, and `f` to switch between descendant and whole-folder classification. Whole-folder mode evaluates folder rules in Simple mode and adds Jev folder classification in Jev mode. `/` filters, `space` skips an operation, `h` opens history, and `?` shows the full key guide. Apply, undo, and redo use confirmation dialogs.

`run` builds its plan in memory and does not create a plan file. It asks for confirmation in a terminal; use `--no-confirm` for explicit non-interactive execution and `--dry-run` to inspect the in-memory plan without moving anything. Use the separate `plan` and `apply` commands when the plan must be reviewed, retained, or applied later.

Running `jev-sort` without a command opens the UI only when stdin and stdout are terminals. Planning never moves source files; `apply` revalidates source fingerprints and destinations before moving anything.

The default user configuration is `${UserConfigDir}/jev-file-sort/config.yaml`. An explicit configuration can be supplied with `--config`.

```yaml
version: 1
mode: simple
scan:
  recursive: true
folders:
  rules_enabled: true
output:
  root: Sorted
  collision: skip
  layout: preserve
rules:
  - id: project-folders
    enabled: true
    kinds: [folder]
    match:
      patterns: ["project-*"]
      depth: { min: 0, max: 1 }
    category: documents
  - id: preset-text
    enabled: false
    kinds: [file]
    category: text
jev:
  concurrency: 4
  batch_size: 100
  folder_evaluation:
    enabled: false
    max_entries: 100
  content:
    enabled: false
    allow_patterns: []
    max_bytes: 32768
```

Rules can target `file`, `folder`, or both. A matching folder rule moves the folder as one unit and does not classify its children individually. Override a built-in rule by using its rule ID, such as `preset-text`, and setting `enabled: false`.

`output.layout: preserve` keeps the source-relative directories below each category, so files such as `internal/config/types.go` and `internal/execute/types.go` remain distinct. Set it to `flatten` to place every classified file directly below its category.

## Jev

Store a TypeSafe API key in the OS credential store, or set `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` for CI:

```sh
jev-sort auth login
jev-sort plan ~/Downloads --mode jev --out plan.json
```

File content is never sent unless content is enabled in the configuration, the file matches an allow pattern, and `plan` is invoked with `--allow-content`. Jev folder evaluation sends folder metadata and a bounded summary of direct children; it can either categorize the whole folder or continue into its children.

Jev mode applies deterministic rules first and only sends unresolved entries to the API. Unresolved siblings are submitted as multiple questions in a shared request, split by `jev.batch_size`, with up to `jev.concurrency` batches in flight. Requests rejected for token size are divided automatically. This keeps common extensions local while retaining semantic classification for ambiguous names and content.

## License

This project is licensed under the MIT License. See the [LICENSE](LICENSE) file for details.

# Crush 好感监控器（本机版）

一个用 Jev 分析你和 Crush、或对象聊天的小工具。帮你读懂一点对方的情绪和想法，也看看自己的回复哪里没表达好、可以怎么调整。

**本版本机运行**：没有账号、没有登录、没有服务器端数据库。装在自己电脑上，用**你自己的 API Key**，聊天记录存在浏览器本地、不上传任何第三方平台（分析时会把相关片段发给模型服务商，见下）。

> ⚠️ **这份代码是 AI 写的**：除了上游原作者那一版，本仓库全部改动由 AI 完成，维护者不懂编程。**遇到问题请直接让 AI 去修**（怎么写、看哪份文档，见 [DISCLAIMER.md](DISCLAIMER.md)）。
>
> 来源与致谢见 [NOTICE.md](NOTICE.md)（**上游作者是 FerryCorleone，功劳是他的**）；数据流向、隐私边界与免责条款见 [PRIVACY.md](PRIVACY.md)。

## 特点

- **微信风格界面**：还原聊天气泡，分析结果直接显示在消息下方。
- **情绪与意图**：每句两行标签，从 12 类情绪、35 类意图中分别展示概率最高的三项。
- **好感度与回复评级**：顶部显示好感信号评分，自己的回复按 SSS 到 D 分档，并给出下一步建议。
- **深度解读（可选，默认关闭）**：接入第二层模型，把这段交流里值得注意的信号整理成「发生了什么 / 和她平时相比 / 你可能漏掉的信号 / 可能是什么意思 / 为什么这么判断 / 目前不能确定 / 接下来观察什么」。填了 DeepSeek Key 再打开。
- **长期观察**：按人记录她自己的行为基线（回复快慢、长短、主动程度等），下次不再从零开始，而是能看出「这一次和她平时哪里不同」。**数字全部由程序计算，模型只负责解释。**
- **历史对话**：每段聊天单独记录、按最近更新排序，随时可以点回去看当时的内容**和已经分析好的标签**（不会重新花钱调模型）；「开始新对话」只新开一段，**不删除任何历史**；每段都能改名。
- **语音 / 图片 / 表情包可补描述**：微信复制出来只有占位符，在占位符后面补一句描述，AI 才知道那是转述而不是原文（见下）。
- **粘贴后不自动分析**：输入框足够大，可以先把描述补好、错字改掉，确认无误再点「分析聊天」。
- **不静默失败**：任何「点了没反应」都会在页面顶部用红条写明原因，并写进本机日志（只记错误文本，不记聊天内容）。

## 长期观察有什么、没有什么

**有**：她平时回复大概多快多长、会不会主动开口、有哪些口头禅、几次对话里反复出现的模式、你亲自确认过的事实、以及你在这个账号下的反馈记录。

**没有**：人格诊断、依恋类型标签、「她喜欢你」的概率、情绪操纵建议、自动发消息或自动回复。

**长期模式只由程序统计产生**（至少 3 段对话支持，涉及一起活动这类解释需要 4 段）；模型自己的推测**永远不会**自动写成长期结论，只有你确认过的才会被记成事实。被你的纠正推翻的推断不会删除，以后可以复盘。

历史样本不足时（少于 3 次对话）系统会直接说明，不会假装已经认识这个人。

## 为什么用 Jev

Jev 是 TypeSafe 推出的结构化判断模型，直接返回分类、评分和概率。这款工具主要需要逐句判断，不需要生成长篇回答，正好适合它的输出方式；情绪和意图也可以放在同一次请求里并行分析。

- [创始人 Diogo Almeida 的 Jev 首发推文（2026-09-15）](https://x.com/CompleteSkeptic/status/2099925682726002904)
- [官方模型介绍](https://typesafe.ai/blog/introducing-system-one-models-and-jev)
- [申请 API Key：TypeSafe 控制台](https://console.typesafe.ai/)

## 不懂代码也能用（大多数人是这样用的）

这个项目本来就是被一个**不懂编程的人**用 AI 做出来的，所以它也是按"让 AI 帮你装"来写的。你有两条路：

**第一条：把仓库链接丢给你的 AI。** 对 Claude / DeepSeek / ChatGPT 说：

> 帮我装这个：https://github.com/yzyialy/crush-monitor —— 按 README 的步骤来，我不会写代码，每一步都告诉我该敲什么、看到什么算成功。

它会一步步带你装好（装 Node、跑 `npm ci`、填 API Key、启动、打开网页）。**报错也不用你懂**：把报错原文贴给它就行。

**第二条：自己照下面的三步做。** 命令可以直接复制粘贴，不需要看懂。

无论哪条路，最麻烦的一步都只是"申请一个 TypeSafe API Key"（要注册账号、拿 Key）——这一步可以让 AI 带你做。

## 快速开始

### 需要什么

| 项 | 要求 |
|---|---|
| Node.js | **22.12 或更高**（建议 24 LTS） |
| TypeSafe API Key | 必需，第一层分析用。[申请地址](https://console.typesafe.ai/) |
| DeepSeek API Key | 可选，只有想用「深度解读」才需要 |

不需要服务器、不需要域名、不需要数据库。

### 装起来（3 分钟）

```sh
# 1. 装依赖
npm ci --include=dev

# 2. 生成 .env（已存在则不会覆盖），然后填入自己的 Key
npm run setup
#   TYPESAFE_API_KEY=your_api_key
#   HOST=127.0.0.1        # 建议就用默认值，只允许本机访问
#   PORT=3178

# 3. 构建前端并启动
npm run build
npm start
```

打开 **http://127.0.0.1:3178/** 就能用了。使用时保持终端运行；下次只要 `npm start`。改了 Key 重启即可。

不想构建也行，开发模式更省事：

```sh
npm run dev            # 打开 http://127.0.0.1:5178/
```

> **请用 `127.0.0.1` 或 `localhost` 打开。** 这个版本没有登录，如果改成让局域网/公网访问（`HOST=0.0.0.0`），任何能连上这个端口的人都能看到你的聊天记录，而且明文 HTTP 下密码类信息会被抓包——虽然本版没有登录，仍**强烈建议只监听本机**。要用别的设备看，用 SSH 端口转发：`ssh -L 3178:127.0.0.1:3178 你的电脑`，然后本机访问 `http://127.0.0.1:3178/`。

## 怎么用

1. 在电脑版微信里多选聊天记录，复制并粘贴到网页输入框。
2. 选择哪个昵称是你，点「分析聊天」（第一次会问你哪个昵称是你，选完点「开始分析」）。
3. 查看情绪、意图和回复评级，点击标签展开详情。
4. 有新聊天时继续粘贴，结果会随上下文更新；想换一段就点「开始新对话（保留历史）」，旧的在顶部「历史对话」里随时能翻回去。

支持微信的「昵称 → 时间 → 正文」格式，也支持 `我：…` / `对方：…`。**仅分析你粘贴的文字，不读取微信数据库、不后台监听。**

### 语音、图片、表情包怎么让 AI 知道

微信复制出来的语音、图片、表情包只有 `[语音]`、`[图片]`、`[动画表情]` 这样的占位，正文是看不见的。**在占位后面直接写一句描述就行**：

```
对方 21:00
[语音] 她说周末要加班，可能来不了

对方 21:02
[图片] 一张加班工位照片，屏幕上全是代码

对方 21:04
[动画表情] 一只猫笑得打滚
```

- 补了描述 → 会被当成「这条消息的内容」参与分析，气泡下方会标出「语音 / 图片 / 表情包 · 你补充的描述」，AI 收到的说明是「这是用户手动转述，不是原始文字」。
- 不补描述 → 跳过、不参与分析，气泡下方会标出「没有补充内容，这条不会参与分析」。
- 统计口径只认你写的那段描述，不带 `[语音]` 这类标记，所以「回复长度」之类的数字不会被占位符撑大。

### 历史对话 / 开始新对话

- 顶部「**历史对话 N**」列出这个人的全部聊天段：每段显示 `第 N 段 · 时间 · 第一句摘要`、条数、最近一条时间；当前那段标「当前」。
- 点任意一段 → 把当时的内容**和已经分析好的标签**调回界面（不重新调用模型，不花额度）。
- 「改名」给某段起个好记的名字（留空恢复自动命名）；「删除」只删那一段，要二次确认。
- 「开始新对话（保留历史）」= 新开一段空的记录，**不删除任何历史**，旧的在列表里随时能回去。

## 隐私与数据

- 聊天记录、分析标签、长期观察档案全部存在**你这台电脑的浏览器 localStorage** 里；换浏览器、无痕窗口、清理浏览数据都会丢，**也没有跨设备同步**（本机版没有服务端）。
- API Key 只在你本机 `.env` 文件里，**永不下发到浏览器**；仓库有测试盯着这条。
- 分析时会把相关聊天片段发给 TypeSafe（用深度解读时还会发给 DeepSeek），这是工具工作的前提。
- 详细的数据流向、第三方接收方、以及"这个工具不会做什么"见 **[PRIVACY.md](PRIVACY.md)**。

## 排障

| 现象 | 处理 |
|---|---|
| 页面打不开 | 确认终端还在跑、地址是 `http://127.0.0.1:3178/` |
| 点「分析聊天」或「开始分析」没反应 | **看页面顶部的红条**——现在所有失败都会写明原因；同时日志在 `logs/server.log` |
| 报 `crypto.randomUUID is not a function` | 说明你在用**明文 HTTP + 非 localhost** 的地址打开（比如局域网 IP）。这类浏览器 API 只在安全上下文存在。改用 `127.0.0.1` 或 SSH 端口转发 |
| 分析报「聊天结构或长度不符合要求」 | 单次别贴太长，或用「继续粘贴」分批 |
| 「深度解读」按钮不可用 | 需要在 `.env` 里填 `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` 并设置 `DEEP_ANALYSIS_ENABLED=true`，然后重启 |
| 换电脑/清缓存后记录没了 | localStorage 是本机、单浏览器绑定；本机版没有同步机制 |

## 开发

React 19 + TypeScript + Vite + Express，使用 TypeSafe SDK 调用 `jev-1.13.0`，深度解读通过官方 Responses API 调用 DeepSeek。

```sh
npm run dev        # 开发模式：http://127.0.0.1:5178/
npm test           # 全部测试：离线、不调用任何真实模型、不花额度
npm run check:live # 真实模型调用检查（会消耗你自己的 TypeSafe 额度）
npm run build      # 类型检查 + 构建前端到 dist/
```

**改代码前请先读 [`docs/AI-HANDOFF.md`](docs/AI-HANDOFF.md)**——那是写给 AI 的交接书（文件职责表、硬规则、常见改动索引、踩过的坑）。设计权威是 [`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md)。

三条最容易被踩坏的红线：

1. **LLM 不得计算或改写任何数字**——基线、趋势、delta、模式只能来自 `shared/patterns.ts` 与 `shared/profile.ts` 的纯函数；
2. **`model_inferred` 永不自动升级为 `user_confirmed`**——只有用户确认能提升来源等级；
3. **失败必须说出来**——任何"点了没反应"的路径都要么显示原因、要么写进日志，不许静默吞掉。

## 目录一览

```
src/       前端（React）
shared/    前后端共用的纯逻辑：解析、统计、基线、模式、记忆、检索、翻译、哈希
server/    本机后端：Express 入口 + 两个模型 provider（Key 只在这里）
tests/     node:test 用例（离线可跑）
scripts/   建 env、真实模型检查、使用说明构建
docs/      架构设计、AI 交接书、使用者说明、本机运行与排障
public/    静态资源与生成的使用说明页
```
